cells.tense: You're moving toward something and you can hold it without gripping it.
cells.ask: Say the goal out loud as something you want, not something you're doing, and let it land that way.
cells.core:
The feeling and the direction are running side by side. You can be moved by where you're headed without turning it into a plan, and someone watching would see you choosing the next step from a place that isn't braced. That's most of why the goal still pulls instead of just pushes, and it's not a trick you're doing — it's where you're standing.

The ask isn't to be softer than you are. Say one want out loud, plainly, without folding it into the next move. You'll hear which goals still have feeling in them and which ones you're only servicing. Either answer is useful, and neither is a failure.
cells.sheetLine: You can be moved by where you're going without gripping the wheel.
cells.place: on the way to something you're actually steering toward

cells.tense: You're bracing for the moment it goes wrong before you've even left the starting line.
cells.ask: Say what you want from this once, not what you'll do when it fails, and then take one step.
cells.core:
You want the thing, you take the step, and the outcome stays open long enough to be lived in — that's the version of this that works. Here, the same direction is being held with a tighter grip, and you're rehearsing the collapse before the climb. Every way it could fail gets mapped before you've moved.

The rehearsing is doing a job, maybe keeping you ahead of the blow, but it's crowding out the feeling that made you want this at all. Say the want once, not the contingency plan, and take a single step in plain daylight. You'll get back the direction you actually chose, and the push will have less to push against.
cells.sheetLine: You're managing the landing before you've left the ground.
cells.place: on the way to something you're actually steering toward

cells.tense: You're standing behind a door that already closed, looking at the handle.
cells.ask: Name one fresh want out loud today, with the honesty of a beginner, and let yourself not know the rest.
cells.core:
You can start something without the whole map, and the goal is allowed to pull you rather than only being something to finish. That ease is still somewhere in you. Where you're standing, the direction is here but the aliveness isn't — you can finish things without letting them reach you, so the goal has less to pull on.

That flatness might be protecting something worth keeping; that's a real possibility, not a verdict. Name one fresh want, simply, without dressing it up in old evidence. You'll find out whether there's a direction that still has a beginner in it. If the answer is none today, that too is something to use.
cells.sheetLine: You can aim at something without it being able to reach you.
cells.place: on the way to something you're actually steering toward

cells.tense: You're already being moved by where this is going, and you're calling it just doing the math.
cells.ask: Say out loud one thing you're heading toward because it still moves you, and call it by that name.
cells.core:
A direction that's steering you and known as yours looks like this: you say what you're after and feel the pull in the saying, and the goal has a name and a heat to it that you'd defend if asked. Here, the pull is still running — it shows in the choices you keep making — but you've filed it under the practical heading.

The steering is real whether or not you claim it, and it's shaping where you land. Say one move you're making because the thing still matters, and name it that way. You aren't performing for anybody; this is just the record catching up to a direction that's already yours.
cells.sheetLine: The direction is yours. You've just been filing it under logistics.
cells.place: on the way to something you're actually steering toward
